title: Internal dual and exact Hom of a finite-free retract sheaf
statement:
Let $(C,J,R)$ be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. In the category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $T$ have maps $i:T\to R^{\oplus r}$ and $p:R^{\oplus r}\to T$ with $r\geq0$ finite and $pi=1_T$. Write $T^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(T,R)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The dual maps give a splitting
$$T^\vee\xrightarrow{p^\vee}(R^{\oplus r})^\vee\xrightarrow{i^\vee}T^\vee,\qquad i^\vee p^\vee=1,$$
and the coordinate-dual identification $(R^{\oplus r})^\vee\cong R^{\oplus r}$ makes this a finite-free retract. For the standard vectors $u_j$ and coordinates $u_j^*$ put $t_j=p(u_j)$ and $\lambda_j=u_j^*i$. On every localized site these satisfy
$$\sum_{j=1}^r t_j\lambda_j=1_T,\qquad \phi=\sum_{j=1}^r\phi(t_j)\lambda_j\quad(\phi\in T^\vee).$$
The canonical sheaf map $\delta_T:T\to(T^\vee)^\vee$, $t\mapsto(\phi\mapsto\phi(t))$, is an isomorphism with inverse $\alpha\mapsto\sum_j\alpha(\lambda_j)t_j$. The functor $\mathcal Hom_R(T,-)$ is naturally a retract of $\mathcal Hom_R(R^{\oplus r},-)\cong(-)^{\oplus r}$ by precomposition with $p$ and $i$, and it sends every short exact sequence of module sheaves to a short exact sequence. All displayed maps and identities commute with restriction to localized sites.
